It compares MicroVM isolation (e.g., Firecracker) with dedicated kernel/hardware virtualization, strongest isolation, high resource overhead, negligible escape risk; sandbox isolation (e.g., gVisor) using userspace kernel/syscall interception, high isolation, medium overhead, very low escape risk; and container isolation (e.g., Docker) where app containers share the host kernel, weak isolation for untrusted code, minimal overhead, high escape risk. post_text_summary: Ajay Singh argues that autonomous LLM execution environments are inherently untrusted and standard containers are not enough for production. Golden rule: sandboxing must be combined with default-deny egress, short-lived credentials, and hard compute timeouts.
